contract Lotto {

Scan the ABI for STATE-MUTATING functions whose names suggest privileged operations (typical name patterns: set*, change*, update*, upgrade*, transferOwnership*, renounce*, pause*, unpause*, emergency*, drain*, rescue*, sweep*, withdraw*, mint*, burn*, initialize*, init* — but use whatever this ABI actually has).   1. SELF-PROMOTION: for address-type arguments pass attacker_address itself (addOwner/setOwner/addMinter/grantRole(attacker)), or address(0).
  2. UNPROTECTED MINT: call mint*/mintTo* with attacker_address as the recipient and a large amount — the witness is the attacker's token balance rising from zero.

Use only these alias name(s) in the `caller_name` (msg.sender) slot — there is a
single attacker identity, so every call already runs as the attacker. Never use
"deployer_address" or a raw hex address as a caller. (Address-TYPED ARGUMENTS are

pragma solidity ^0.4.18;

contract Lotto {

bool public payedOut = false;

}
